topic: A person discovers the tree they planted as a child has been cut down
text: I walk slowly, almost hesitantly, towards the spot where the tree once stood. It's hard to believe what I'm seeing – just a stump, a small reminder of what was once a towering presence. This tree, a sapling when I was just a kid, was more than just a plant. It was a connection to my childhood, a silent witness to my growth, my dreams, my secrets. Now, it’s just a rough circle of wood, a stark contrast to the vibrant life it once led. The air feels a bit thinner here without the canopy that used to shade this exact spot. I trace the rings on the stump, each one a year of life, a year of memory. How will I fill this void?
